title: Mumbai-Based Wiffy Raises $3 Million to Expand AI-Powered Home Services Platform
excerpt: The Series A round, led by Earth Fund with participation from Japan's Persol Holdings, will help Wiffy scale its post-purchase installation and maintenance network across India.
body:
• Wiffy has raised $3 million in Series A funding led by Earth Fund, with Japan's Persol Holdings and existing backer Capria Ventures joining the round.
  • The Mumbai-based startup operates a full-stack platform connecting consumer durables brands with trained technicians for post-purchase installation and maintenance across 300+ Indian cities.
  • Funds will go toward AI-powered workforce management tools, enterprise partnerships, and expansion into new service categories.

Wiffy, a Mumbai-based startup that manages post-purchase installation and servicing for home improvement and consumer durables brands, has raised $3 million in a Series A funding round. Earth Fund led the round, with Japan's Persol Holdings and existing investor Capria Ventures also participating, according to VCCircle.

The company said it will deploy the capital to strengthen its technology platform, build out AI-driven workforce management capabilities, deepen enterprise partnerships, and push into new product categories beyond its core home improvement vertical.

From Installations to a Full-Stack Service Layer

Founded in 2019 by Vikram Sharma and Deepanshu Goel, Wiffy — formally Installco WIFY Technology Private Limited — started as a platform for on-site installation services. It has since evolved into a full-stack B2B2C operation that handles everything from workflow management to after-sales support for brands selling products that need professional setup at customer homes.

https://x.com/entrackr/status/2080250868817924160

Its client roster spans large enterprises like IKEA, Amazon, Godrej, and Panasonic as well as mid-market home design companies such as Livspace and Homelane. The platform now supports more than 4,700 trained technicians operating across 300-plus cities in India and claims to have served over one million households to date.

"This investment will accelerate our mission to be a key contributor to the #ViksitBharat vision, empowering millions of tradesmen in the home improvement industry while serving both brands and households."

— Vikram Sharma, Co-Founder and CEO, Wiffy

Tapping a $30 Billion Market

Wiffy operates in what Capria Ventures estimates is a $30 billion home improvement market in India, with a serviceable addressable opportunity of roughly $3 billion. The gap between rising consumer expectations for professional installation and the fragmented, largely unorganized workforce that delivers those services is what the startup is trying to close.

India is not a DIY market in the way that Western economies are. Consumers purchasing anything from modular kitchens and air conditioners to smart home devices typically depend on third-party technicians for installation and ongoing maintenance. Brands, meanwhile, struggle to ensure consistent quality when outsourcing last-mile service to local contractors. Wiffy positions itself as the connective layer — vetting, training, and dispatching technicians through its platform while giving brands real-time visibility into service delivery.

AI and Workforce Management at the Core

A significant chunk of the new funding is earmarked for AI-powered workforce tools. The company's platform already handles technician allocation, scheduling, and performance tracking, but the next phase aims to automate more of these decisions — matching the right technician to a job based on skill set, geography, and availability, while reducing turnaround times.

The Wiffy Partner App, available on Indian app stores, lets carpenters, electricians, plumbers, and other skilled workers receive verified job assignments directly, without middlemen. The company says payments are guaranteed, a feature designed to build trust and reduce attrition in a sector where informal arrangements and delayed payments are common.

Backing from Diverse Investors

The startup has now raised a total of approximately $7.7 million across multiple rounds. Earlier backers include Blume Ventures, Pidilite Ventures (the investment arm of adhesives giant Pidilite Industries), Mount Judi Ventures, and Singularity Growth. Pidilite's involvement is particularly strategic — as a major supplier to India's construction and home improvement trade, it has a direct interest in improving last-mile service quality.

The entry of Japan's Persol Holdings signals growing cross-border interest in India's field services sector. Persol, a major staffing and HR technology conglomerate, operates extensively in workforce solutions across Asia — a natural fit for a company building technology-driven labor management at scale.

What to Watch

Wiffy reported revenue of over ₹34 crore in FY24, according to Inc42. With the Series A capital, the company plans to expand beyond home improvement into adjacent categories such as commercial spaces and smart home ecosystems. The bet is that the same platform architecture — trained technicians, tech-enabled dispatch, brand integration — can be replicated across verticals where professional installation and maintenance are critical.

Sharma, a Harvard Business School alumnus who previously founded and exited Carcrew to the TVS Group, is joined by COO Deepanshu Goel, a Carnegie Mellon Tepper MBA with operating experience at Amazon. The founding team's playbook is clear: professionalize India's fragmented field services market one vertical at a time, with AI doing the heavy lifting on allocation and quality control.
nri_angle: Wiffy's expansion into AI-powered home services could interest diaspora investors and NRIs looking at India's rapidly growing consumer services sector.
author: Diaspora Desk
